title: In Vitro Culture and Live Imaging of Mouse Embryonic Sternums
protocol: Cross mice B6.129\(Cg)-Gt\(ROSA)26Sortm4\(ACTB-tdTomato,-EGFP)Luo/J with mice FVB.Cg-Tg\(CAG-cre/Esr1) 5Amc/J.
Record the plugging time in the morning and count it as E0.5.
Dissolve tamoxifen in corn oil at a concentration of 20 mg/ml by adding 100 μl of 100% ethanol to 20 mg tamoxifen, then let it soak for 5 minutes before adding corn oil.
Intraperitoneally inject pregnant mice with tamoxifen at a dose of 1.2 mg per mouse on E10.5.
Sacrifice pregnant mice by E12.5 or E13.0 and save the embryos in PBS solution.
Examine the embryos under ZEISS Stemi SV 11 Apo microscope using GFP excitation illumination.
Save GFP positive embryos in CO2-independent medium \(Gibico, Cat. # 18045).
Dissect GFP positive embryos in CO2-independent medium to recover sternums.
Cut the head off first along the neck.
Under dissecting microscope, cut muscles with covering skin along the left side of the backbone and carefully remove them from the backbone.
Peel muscles together with skin along the rib cage toward the sternum until most of the skin is peeled after passing the left side sternum.
Repeat the procedure for the right side, ensuring that muscles/skin are removed as a single unit.
Trim off the lower trunk part from the muscle/skin peeled chest.
Cut all left and right ribs near the sternum with micro-dissecting forceps to release the sternum with attached rib parts.
Ensure the attached left and right side ribs are roughly symmetrical, trimming extra parts if necessary.
Set up the in vitro culture device.
Trim the Costar Transwell insert wall.
Place the trimmed insert into a ø50mm culture dish.
Put two L-shaped capillary-micropipets between the insert bottom and the culture dish glass cover.
Wet the Costar Transwell insert mesh with DMEM/F12 culture medium containing 10% fetal bovine serum plus 1x antibiotics and antimycotics.
Lay the sternum on the insert so that the skin/ventral side touches the mesh.
Suck off extra medium to ensure the sternum touches down firmly on the mesh.
Adjust the sternum with forceps to make sure it is fully stretched gently on the mesh surface.
Fill the space beneath the mesh with culture medium, ensuring only immersion of the sternum in the medium.
Culture the set-up sternums in a conventional cell culture incubator for a few hours or overnight at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Transfer the in vitro culture system to the cell culture chamber of PerkinElmer spinning disc confocal microscope.
Set the culture conditions to 37°C and 5% CO2.
Discern the location of the sternum as well as its top and bottom under dim transmitted light.
Take live images from 6 to 10 hours, at 1.5 or 2 µm z-spacing with a time interval of 5 minutes using a 20x objective lens with long working distance (3.5 mm) and water immersion.
Use both transmitted light and 488 nm laser to visualize sternums contour and individual GFP-positive sternum cells respectively.
Return the in vitro culture system to a conventional cell culture incubator after live imaging is finished.
Change the culture medium every two days for further culture.
Keep the culture growing for up to one week.
Analyze live images with Volocity software.
